title: Gave it a shot - Opus 5.5 + Blender + Unreal Engine + Meshy
author: edm-4-life
selftext:
I was inspired by some recent posts. Finally connected via MCP and let Claude drive everything.  
Workflow: Plan, get reference images, connect MCP to both and log into Meshy on built-in browser, feed to Claude, and this is what we go after less than 10 updates. I'm pretty impressed with Claude.

Not a game designer by any sort, feedback welcome!

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: Just curious, why UE and not Godot?

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body: Saw someone post the other day using UE and just decided to try it. Used Godot before but decided to do UE for this project.

comments.author: pricetag
comments.body:
hey i made it before the brigade of everyone saying its a walking simulator. 

looks good OP but is it 'actually a game' or so they ask?

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body: ya, i had CLaude develop a plan, so we're working on mechanics now and then NPCs and quests, then expand the world...it's a process i guess

comments.author: Overall-Suit-5531
comments.body: Very nice!! I am interested in trying something similar, approximately what has been the cost up to this point?

comments.author: vanidmt
comments.body: Yeah, it's amazing, but my problem is: what's the next step if everyone can do this? What will be the way to make this game interesting and playable for real players?

replies.body: That’s the hard part, a little of familiar styles of play that’s known to work. I feel like getting gear and some competitive elements to it would be a bigger draw vs story.

comments.author: JirayaaaBoyy106

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body: Workflow is in the post. I gave full access to blender,  Unreal Engine, and Meshy and it did everything

comments.author: warrior5715
comments.body: What prompt did u use? Is it one shot or multiple iterations?

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body:
I showed it a few recent UE based demos from reddit, said I wanted a demo where I can run around to explore and to add a little legend of zelda touch to it. That helps explain that little elephant that follows me around (instead of a fairy). And, I said spend no more than 45 minutes on it. That was the first pass. It gave me what i wanted with a crash test dummy type character that I could explore the forest with.

Then, I told it to start making models, provided a reference image, and it went to work. Honestly, it was pretty good after the 2nd pass. The few after was to add a small village and allow for interchangeable gear. It said it would split the character up into 4 pieces and that worked pretty well, next was making sure it gripped the weapon well and added attack...etc

Hope that helps you get started.

comments.author: Same_Opposite6306
comments.body:
How many tokens did it cost, or percentage of your plan? How long did claude take for your first working prototype?  
I am already having trouble getting a functional terrain LOD streaming system up and running.

replies.author: edm-4-life
replies.body: This one, cost about 25% of my total weekly on a max plan. And, after the planning and having it generate me a reference image, I specifically told it to keep it under 45 minutes and it did. I was able to get a crash test dummy character and a forest with a path. I added a campfire and village in the 2nd pass.
